items.title: Terry Clark — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The group started out with Basie, Gus Johnson on drums, Jimmie Lewis... and Freddie Green, of course, guitar. In the front line was me...

ctx.x: . . . a bigger part of the fee.

They wanted to get Basie out of debt, so they put a small band around him, paid him a small salary. As a matter of fact, Buddy DeFranco, the clarinet player – caucasian cat. You know who he is – he was making more money than Basie was, and they put him in Basie’s band. The group started out with Basie, Gus Johnson on drums, Jimmie Lewis, who is a bass violin player that we had run into in Louisville, Kentucky, and Freddie Green, of course, guitar. In the front line was me, Buddy DeFranco, and a saxophone player.…
We opened at a place called – right in . . .

items.title: Clark Terry interviewed by Joe Williams and Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, May 19, 1995
items.q: me and Basie and Freddie, we’d load his whole salary and more... I was making with Basie $125 a week... Freddie Green opens his door... Freddie, I walked in... Pep would look at you like this

ctx.x: Yeah, you know, what am I telling you? Well we’re playing Wilkes Barre, Pennsylvania, and this was during a period when we were not allowed to stay in the big hotel, we were relegated to the homes of Miss Brown, Miss Jones, Miss Green and so forth.
Oh, those were the good old days. “Have you had your breakfast?” “No, M’am.”

items.title: 68097_Freddie Green oral history interview
items.q: [INTERVIEWEE] Let's see. Clark Terry. ... And Clark Terry. And, Marshall, and myself.

ctx.x: And, Clark Terry. Was that the break?
